data.title: The site takes the command reference as a committed file, not a build-time download
data.why: A site deploy happens far more often than a release, and a build that fetches a release asset to describe a command can fail for a reason nobody changed. As a committed file the reference shows up in a pull request diff, so a version bump shows exactly which flags moved. Freshness is checked, not hoped for: the generator refuses to run when reference.json and facts.json disagree about the version.
data.rejected: Fetch the release artifact at build time, as T60 assumed — right in spirit, fragile once per deploy; Depend on the kadence package and run its generator: the best of the three, but only once a published version carries the generator
